item.title: El que se va sin que lo boten, regresa sin que lo llamen.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: A figure with a suitcase walks away, then hesitantly peeks back through the door. People who leave on their own often return without an invite.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"El que se va sin que lo boten, regresa sin que lo llamen."
❓ You give up your standing when you walk out by choice. Then you lose your leverage if you try to return uninvited. A voluntary exit costs you power if you ever try to return. Imagine an employee who resigns, then seeks re-employment. Or a partner who leaves a relationship, then tries to reconcile uninvited. They come back now on their terms, not yours.
AND: You recognize it as the quiet DM months later, or the classic warning whispered by family. A former colleague who quit in a huff quietly slides into your DMs, asking if the old role is still open. Family members also whisper a warning after a relative cuts ties over a minor dispute, only to show up at Thanksgiving dinner as if nothing happened.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • You will come crawling back. • They always come back. • The grass is not always greener.

item.title: Stability Is a Setting
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Red Impulsiveness and Reality Detachment get handled as a messaging problem first. The public readout is updated so the board deck can still show Leadership Confidence: Stable.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Stability Is a Setting"
❓ Red warning gauges get treated as a comms problem so early structural change can wait. Continuity is cheaper than correction, so by the time a real fix arrives, the gap between the public story and day-to-day reality is already wide.
AND: When the Grandiosity Gauges show high impulsiveness, the first move is usually to update the public readout. Grandiose thinking gets reframed as strategic intent so the board deck can match last quarter. Keeping the current leadership costs less, short term, than opening a search. The board can file the red needles under communication risk rather than leadership failure, which delays the audit. When correction finally arrives, it is often a late restructure after Leadership Confidence: Stable has already bought time.

item.title: Public Money, Private Leverage
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: A concentrated group tracks the rules and presses for the next exception. The cost is spread so thin that almost nobody follows every transfer.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Public Money, Private Leverage"
❓ Tax money enters at one end and comes back as lobbying power at the other. The public funds the loop, then meets it again at the ballot box.
AND: Incentives can build a closed loop between public money, private advantage, and political pull. A small group has the time, skill, and cash to chase the next exception. Everyone else eats a cost spread so thin that almost nobody tracks the transfer. They dress the gears in subsidy, partnership, competitiveness, reform. It can look professional even when public money helps pay for the influence that protects the payout. The smaller the group that wins, the louder it comes back to press again. Without honest, independently watched conflict-of-interest rules, the machine keeps paying the people who keep the gears turning.
🟣 W19: Reptilocracy 🦎🏛️
Reptilocracy is a cartoon stopwatch on cold-blooded leaders in suits. We still let untested nervous systems run big institutions. When public money comes back as private leverage, the people who keep the loop running look like the adults in the room.

item.title: 🪞 Why does the brain keep selling you a new "me"?
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Your sense of self is a brain construct: the brain blends what it already expects with what the senses pick up now, and you take that mix as who you are. Your inner voice helps you plan and turn events into a story of who you are. When that voice loops as chatter (rumination and catastrophizing), you replay the same worry without solving anything. Upbringing and a negativity bias (bad news hits harder than good) …
item.sync:pageSocial:
🪞 Why does the brain keep selling you a new "me"?
A stable "me" is a live mix. Heather Berlin, Ethan Kross, and Nicole Vignola argue the brain mixes what it already expects with what the senses pick up now, and that mix can shift when you change what you attend to and the story you tell about yourself.
✜ You pull the evidence your mood already wants Mood decides what you notice, even when the kitchen has not changed. A negative headspace pulls more negative evidence. You live inside a perception box: a bounded window you treat as the whole world.
✜ The voice writes the plot, then it can loop Your inner voice helps you plan and turn events into a story of who you are. When it loops as chatter (rumination and catastrophizing), you replay the same worry without solving anything.
✜ Self-criticism starts as copying You copy what you see in parents and peers, not only what you are told. Bad news lands harder than good, so as an adult you still use those early stories.
Say the story they taught you about yourself, and the story you now tell yourself. Change what you attend to and which stories you repeat, and people who know you start meeting a different version of you.

item.title: El alcahuete es peor que el autor.
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Someone always paves the road. A nod in the meeting, or covering a lie, already puts you in the cover-up.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"El alcahuete es peor que el autor."
❓ The silent enabler who provides the infrastructure carries more blame than the active wrongdoer. The facilitator removes friction, making the infraction possible, not the actor who commits the deed. You use it when a politician defends a corrupt colleague, or when a bystander encourages bullying instead of intervening.
AND: No crime happens in a vacuum; someone always paves the road. You hear it when a colleague nods along to a toxic manager's rant in a meeting, just to stay on their good side. It also comes up when a friend agrees to cover for a partner's lie, and they become part of the cover-up.
🔤 IN ENGLISH: • The one who holds the ladder is worse than the thief • An accessory to the crime is as guilty as the perpetrator • Enabling is worse than doing

item.title: Insert Vote, Receive Same
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Slogans multiply while gatekeepers keep the decision range narrow. Recurring failure then looks like the public picked badly.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Insert Vote, Receive Same"
❓ We can choose which candidate disappoints us, not whether the system will. The vote changes the label; the machine keeps dispensing the same menu.
AND: The window is full of boxes, each a different name for the same letdown. Short-term incentives, donors, gatekeepers, and fear of established interests decide what even gets a slot. Then they sell the ache as a shopping problem: try a different box next time. Recurring failure starts to look like the public chose badly. That is evidence the menu itself is constrained. If every option disappoints, look at the machine. Without basic checks for honesty, courage, and contact with reality, we keep promoting people who fit the slot better than they serve anyone standing in front of it.
🟣 W18: Reptilocracy 🦎🏛️
Reptilocracy is a cartoon stopwatch on cold-blooded leaders in suits. We still let untested nervous systems run big institutions. When the menu never opens, swapping the face at the counter still leaves the same boxes in the window.

item.title: Everyone knows, nobody acts
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Private doubt rarely starts punishment. Groups punish a cheat only when the cheat becomes common knowledge: everyone knows, and everyone knows that everyone knows. Pyramids and thin sideways talk keep that from forming: each person can see the cheat and still stay quiet, because nobody has heard the others say it out loud.
item.sync:pageSocial:
Everyone knows, nobody acts
You can see the cheat from your desk and still do nothing. Your counterpart on another team saw it too. Neither of you has said it out loud, so moving first looks paranoid, rude, or like a career error.
Groups do not punish on private doubt. They punish when everyone knows the cheat, and each person can see that the others know it too. That nested certainty is common knowledge. Without it, private seeing stays stuck.
A public trial works because the room sees that the room got the same message. Hallway gossip leaves you unsure your version matches theirs. People keep nodding along until someone speaks where others can hear that others heard.
Once the company gets big, information climbs and detail dies, so thinking stops at your layer. A con artist only needs each person to think, "Maybe I am the only one who sees this." Sideways talk is thin.
Ten people saw the problem in a cross-team meeting. The VP got one skip-level bullet, trimmed by a director. The cheat sits in what got cut.
In a pyramid, the speech that could flip the room often dies at the next layer. Going first can cost your reputation, your standing, and your relationships. Without a message the whole room hears together, the cheat keeps operating.
#EveryoneKnowsNobodyActs #SharedIllusionsRunTheWorld #RealityCheck #SeeTheGame

item.title: Charisma On, Empathy Off
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: Power redesigns the role so care for the people who bear the cost looks like a bug. Once it is gone, emotional distance gets sold as toughness and maturity.
item.sync:pageSocial:
"Charisma On, Empathy Off"
❓ On the table, they drain empathy out like excess fluid and tick the box for success. The checklist keeps charisma and party loyalty switched on, but turns off the part of us that hurts when others do.
AND: Fear and incentives teach the same lesson: feel too much for the people who bear the cost and you slow the decision, resist the harsh call, or sit with guilt. So the culture splits the smile from the feeling. Charm and slogans stay; real concern goes numb. They rename the distance toughness, objectivity, or putting the mission first, and call the extraction professional maturity. When hurting less matters more than harming less, the system anesthetizes itself. Without filters for real empathy and the courage to act on it, we promote leaders who can smile while their decisions quietly grind other nervous systems down.
🟣 W17: Reptilocracy 🦎🏛️
Reptilocracy is a cartoon stopwatch on cold-blooded leaders in suits. We still let untested nervous systems run big institutions. When the role works better once empathy is drained, the checklist stays green and the people who pay the cost stay off the page.

item.title: 🧩 The structural refusal of a shared timeline
item.dc:creator: xynova
item.description: You put a date or an intent on the table, and the fight goes to chaos instead of closing. Character pathology (Palmatier): a checkable fact can feel like an attack, not help toward agreement. When someone’s false self needs a story that flatters them, hard reality lands as invasion. Emotional reasoning flips the order: I feel attacked by the facts, so you must be attacking me.
item.sync:pageSocial:
🧩 The structural refusal of a shared timeline
You put a date or an intent on the table, and the fight goes to chaos instead of closing. This is less a normal disagreement than two ways of seeing the same scene. One side thinks facts clear things up; the other treats that clarity as something to dodge.
✜ Character pathology Palmatier names the pattern: how someone handles reality and blame. Clinic labels often miss half the behavior or over-label the person. This name points at the habit first. When they refuse the record, facts will not close the fight, and the stated dispute is mostly cover.
✜ Fact as invasion In a normal conflict, a fact clears what is unknown. Here it leaves a trail of rewritten stories. For a false self that cannot survive a mistake, that trail is an inconvenient continuity. When a fact in time proves the error, the floor drops out, and they attack whoever put them on the record.
Feeling becomes proof: "I feel attacked by the facts, so you must be attacking me." They bend reality around the feeling, turn your tone into "evidence," attribute their own defects to you, and drop the facts to focus on their reaction. Rage at an irrefutable fact is fear of losing control of the narrative. The loop only needs to last long enough for accountability to dissolve into a fog of complexity.
You match dates; they build a negotiable reality where truth is optional. Every valid clarification becomes material for the next rewrite.
If you cannot agree what happened, you cannot move on. Better to avoid contact and set limits than burn time on heroic conversations. Any bond that asks you to drop checkable facts for "peace" is broken. That "peace" which denies reality does not hold.
